decision.title: Date formatting: the picture engine over format-integer (packet )
decision.summary: Date and time formatting reuses the format-integer picture engine for each variable marker, scans the picture in three passes, supports the AD and ISO calendars and English names only.

body.p: , after , and . src/format_date.c with the module header src/format_date_internal.h, part src/function_library_format_date.c (part format_date), test format_date.

item.p: One engine: a variable marker's first presentation modifier is a primary format token of the engine; a minimum width widens the digit pattern (optional signs from the right, then prepended digits of the family) and parses it again; non-digit tokens are padded with spaces. Fractional seconds parse the reversed token (so [f#99] is FOFD1340) and write the fraction's digits directly with the effect of 9.9.4.5's reversal ([f,*-2] of .006 is "0", as QT4 expects).

Scan: three passes over the picture (syntax FOFD1340, then components FOFD1350, then writing), so a rejected picture writes nothing. Whitespace in a marker is dropped; the last comma starts the width; a lone "]" is FOFD1340.

Calendar arithmetic on a year of the same 400-year cycle, so day of week, ISO week (W) and week in month (w, the month of the week's Thursday) hold for every int64_t year; W, w and F's numbers follow ISO 8601 in both calendars.

Calendars and languages (): AD (default; year 0 is 1 BC, eras AD/BC) and ISO (absolute year, era "-"). Other designators and any name in a namespace format as AD after "[Calendar: AD]"; a name in no namespace that is no designator, or no EQName, is FOFD1340. A prefix is not resolved (no statically known namespaces at run time): any prefix counts as a namespace. A non-English $language gives "[Language: en]"; the empty sequence or "" gives none (the default language is not read: English whatever the host names). $place is ignored.

Names: English months and days, conventional day abbreviations (Tues, Weds, Thurs/Thur) before cutting at the maximum width; am/pm; AD, BC, ISO always in capitals. Title-case words capitalize after a hyphen ("Twenty-One", QT4 format-date-en125), unlike format-integer's "Twenty-one" (). Timezone names need a database (): [ZN] and other tokens use 01:01; ZZ gives military letters, "J" without a timezone.
Measured (debug driver, XP40): fn-format-date 20 to 124 of 124 run, fn-format-time 19 to 94 of 94, fn-format-dateTime 5 to 80 of 80.
